F-02.baseline: One refresh replacement request; existing refresh replaced.
F-02.candidate: No replacement request at 24,999 ms remaining; existing refresh remains usable; no prompt.
F-02.consequence_limit: No failed recovery observed. Current source arithmetic is confirmed, but early retained refresh is not supplied by the baseline standard Home hide flow.
F-02.recommendation: Downgrade release importance; retain as a scheduling gap with unproven end-user delta.
F-02.next_action: Validate a shared reachable journey or retain as optional robustness correction.

F-03.response_before_login: Baseline clears stale refresh at sign-in; candidate preserves it.
F-03.response_after_login: Both versions install the stale response. That acceptance race is pre-existing.
F-03.deadline_acquisition_control: Baseline acquires session-B refresh and recovers. Candidate reuses session-A refresh, then recovery rejects and clears B.
F-03.no_acquisition_after_login_control: Both versions send session-A refresh and clear B. This user failure is inherited when the replacement callback is absent.
F-03.recommendation: Keep the new/worsened session-boundary finding, but narrow its cause. Do not classify unconditional stale-response installation as newly introduced.
F-03.next_action: Distinguish fresh sign-in from same-session rotation and prevent ended-session responses.
